heroHeadline: PLA Sets New 29-Sortie Non-Exercise Record on May 2 — Surpasses April 26 Peak; J-10, J-16, KJ-500 Deployed; Taiwan Tops Xi's Summit Agenda; 4th Budget Talks May 6; 10 Days to Trump-Xi Beijing Summit
heroSubtitle: PLA aircraft sorties surged to a new non-exercise record of 29 on May 2, 2026 — surpassing the previous high of 28 set on April 26 and the highest count since Justice Mission-2025 (December 2025). Fifteen of 29 sorties crossed Taiwan's median line simultaneously into northern, central, and southwestern ADIZ sectors, with J-10 fighters, J-16 multi-role fighters, and the KJ-500 AEW&C command aircraft deployed. PLA then executed its established spike-then-pullback cycle: 4 sorties (May 1) → 29 sorties (May 2, new record) → 1 sortie (May 3) → 2 sorties (May 4). As of May 4, Taiwan's MND detected 2 sorties (northern + southwestern ADIZ) and 8 PLAN vessels plus 3 official ships — near-baseline air activity but the highest naval count since April 27 (9 vessels), signaling PLA sustains maritime pressure even during air lulls. Taiwan tops Xi Jinping's agenda for the May 14-15 Trump-Xi Beijing summit (10 days away), with Beijing expected to press Trump on arms sales restraint and opposition to Taiwanese independence. Taiwan's fourth cross-party defense budget negotiation round is scheduled for May 6; the KMT remains split between an NT$800B cap and NT$380B alternative while the DPP insists on the full NT$1.25 trillion. A US senator called on Taiwan's legislature to pass the budget as 'a signal to China that Taiwan is serious about peace through strength.'
